source_steps.text: Fix arbitrary x∈ℝ^n and a real t, temporarily assuming L1: t>0. By H002 the component functions are smooth near (x,t). H004 gives u·u=1 in that neighborhood. Differentiating this identity in time by the componentwise product rule gives 2u·u_t=0, hence u·u_t=0. All quantities in this paragraph are evaluated at (x,t).
H005 at (x,t) provides a real a with u_tt−Delta u=a u; choose one. By F001 and symmetry of the inner product, u_t·(u_tt−Delta u)=a(u_t·u)=0. No derivative of a has been taken.

The same twice-differentiated unit constraint gives 0=∂_t²(u·u)=2|u_t|²+2u·u_tt, so u·u_tt=−|u_t|². For each spatial coordinate j from 1 through n, differentiating twice in that coordinate gives 0=2|∂_{x_j}u|²+2u·∂_{x_jx_j}u, so u·∂_{x_jx_j}u=−|∂_{x_j}u|². Dotting the chosen normality equation with u and using u·u=1 yields a=u·u_tt−Σ_j u·∂_{x_jx_j}u=Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|². This calculation uses only the equation for a, and therefore holds for every real scalar satisfying that equation at this point. Substitution gives u_tt−Delta u=(Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|²)u. Combine this with F001 and F002, discharge L1 to retain t>0 as the quantifier condition, and universally quantify x and t. This proves all the asserted pointwise identities and the explicit equation.

Fix real t0 and assume L1: t0>0. Put J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. Its endpoints satisfy 0<t0/2<3t0/2<∞, so H006 provides a compact spatial set for that entire interval. H001 gives finite positive integer dimensions throughout.

Choose such a C from F001. A compact subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space is bounded; enlarging a bound gives a positive real R such that C⊂(−R,R)^n. Compactness also makes C closed, hence (ℝ^n\C)×int J is open. On this open set u=q. By H002 and the local derivative of a constant, every positive-order spatial or time derivative of u vanishes there. Differentiating a constant here uses the fixed vector q and requires no condition on its norm.

Choose R as in F002 and put Q=[−R,R]^n. It is compact and has finite Lebesgue measure |Q|=(2R)^n. By smoothness H002, finite sums and products of the derivatives occurring in e, e_t, u_t·u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u, u_t·∂_{x_j}u and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u) are continuous, and e,e_t are jointly smooth. At every fixed r∈int J each listed spatial function vanishes outside C by F003, and is bounded on Q by continuity on a compact set. Continuous real functions on ℝ^n are measurable; a bound on Q and zero values outside Q dominate their absolute values by a finite constant times the indicator of Q. That indicator is integrable with integral (2R)^n, so each function is absolutely integrable. This applies to every spatial coordinate j with 1≤j≤n, and to every r∈int J.

Define η=t0/4>0. Then [t0−η,t0+η]=[3t0/4,5t0/4]⊂(t0/2,3t0/2)=int J. The continuous real function |e_t| on the compact nonempty set Q×[t0−η,t0+η] is bounded. Taking a nonnegative bound proves that there exists B≥0 with |e_t(x,r)|≤B for every x∈Q and every r in this closed time interval.

Choose B from F004. The witnesses C,R,η,B and defined J,Q have all the asserted common-support, measure, regularity, integrability and bound properties by F001,F002,F003,F005,F004. In particular t0∈int J and e(·,t0) is integrable. Introduce the existential quantifiers over C,R,η,B before closing their scope; discharge L1 and universally quantify the arbitrary t0. This proves the detailed common-support assertion and, by the arbitrariness of the positive base time, integrability of e(·,t) for every t>0.

Fix real t0 and temporarily assume L1: t0>0. Instantiate N002 to choose jointly C,R,η,B, and set J=[t0/2,3t0/2], Q=[−R,R]^n as in that statement. In particular the indicated time window lies in int J. By H002 the product rule and equality of mixed coordinate derivatives give, at every (x,t) with t>0,
e_t(x,t)=2u_t(x,t)·u_tt(x,t)+2Σ_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_j}u(x,t)·∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t).
N002 makes every term on the right integrable at each such time.

For each fixed spatial point x∈Q and each real nonzero increment h0 with |h0|<η, apply M004 to the real function of time r↦e(x,r), extended by zero on nonpositive times, and its derivative r↦e_t(x,r) on positive times (also assigned zero elsewhere). Use the ordered endpoints min(t0,t0+h0), max(t0,t0+h0). Their closed interval lies inside [t0−η,t0+η]⊂int J, where smoothness gives continuity and the stated derivative. M004 gives an intermediate derivative equal to the secant slope. For either sign of h0 that slope is (e(x,t0+h0)−e(x,t0))/h0. The uniform bound in N002 therefore gives its absolute value at most B. Outside Q both densities are zero by N002. Thus throughout ℝ^n,
|(e(x,t0+h0)−e(x,t0))/h0|≤B 1_Q(x).
The right side is integrable, since Q has finite measure and B is finite and nonnegative.

Take an arbitrary real sequence h and temporarily assume L2: for every natural k, 0<|h(k)|<η, and h(k)→0. Define V(k)(x)=(e(x,t0+h(k))−e(x,t0))/h(k) and w(x)=B 1_Q(x). Each V(k) is a continuous real function of x, hence strongly measurable and in particular almost everywhere strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure; it is integrable either by N002 and linearity or by F002. By F002, |V(k)(x)|≤w(x) everywhere, and w is integrable. By the pointwise time differentiability supplied by smoothness, V(k)(x)→e_t(x,t0) for every x. All these facts concern the real codomain and the Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n.

Apply M001 with its measure space ℝ^n with Lebesgue measure, codomain ℝ, sequence V, limit x↦e_t(x,t0), and bound w. The four analytic premises were proved in F003, and ℝ has the required real normed-space structure. It follows that ∫ V(k)(x) dx→∫ e_t(x,t0) dx. N002 and D004 identify, by linearity of finite integrals, ∫ V(k)(x) dx=(E(t0+h(k))−E(t0))/h(k). Discharge L2 and quantify the arbitrary sequence h: every sequence of nonzero increments in this punctured η-window tending to zero gives energy quotients tending to ∫ e_t(x,t0) dx.

F004 implies the full punctured limit as the real increment tends to zero. Indeed failure of that limit would give some fixed positive error and arbitrarily small nonzero increments within the η-window whose quotient errors are at least that amount. Choosing one at distance less than 1/(k+1) for each natural k would form a sequence contradicting F004. This is the sequential criterion for limits in ℝ, with the entire window inside positive time. Thus the actual finite integral E is differentiable at t0 and
E'(t0)=∫_{ℝ^n}e_t(x,t0) dx.
Combine this with F001 and the integrability exported in N002. Discharge L1 and universally quantify t0; no choices C,R,η,B enter the conclusion. This proves the claimed derivative formula and integrability.

Fix real t0 and assume L1: t0>0, and fix any spatial coordinate j with 1≤j≤n (H001). Choose C,R from N002 at this time and set Q=[−R,R]^n. Put g(x)=u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u(x,t0). It is smooth by H002. Since C is compact and contained in the open box (−R,R)^n, it has positive distance from the boundary of Q; N002 therefore makes g zero on a neighborhood of that boundary. The product rule gives
∂_{x_j}g(x)=∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u(x,t0)+u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_jx_j}u(x,t0).
N002 says the derivative and each summand are continuous, supported in C, and integrable on ℝ^n and hence on Q.

Let iota(y,r) insert the real r in coordinate j, with y∈ℝ^(n−1) giving all remaining coordinates in their original order, and put phi(y)(r)=g(iota(y,r)). For each y, phi(y) is smooth on ℝ with derivative r↦∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)). Its endpoint values at −R and R are zero, since those points have a coordinate on the boundary of Q and in any event lie outside C. Apply M003 with real codomain, endpoints −R,R, function phi(y), and the displayed derivative. The derivative exists at every point of [−R,R] and is continuous, hence interval integrable there. We obtain
∫_{−R}^{R} ∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)) dr=phi(y)(R)−phi(y)(−R)=0.
This holds for every y∈ℝ^(n−1). The oriented integral agrees with the Lebesgue integral on the closed interval here, since −R<R and the endpoints have measure zero.

Set Qrest=[−R,R]^(n−1). Under iota, Qrest×[−R,R] is exactly Q with its coordinates reordered. Standard Lebesgue measure is the product of the coordinate measures (D001); reordering these factors preserves the measure, since on any coordinate rectangle both descriptions give the product of the same side lengths. Thus the integral on Q is the product-measure integral of (y,r)↦∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)) with Lebesgue measures restricted to Qrest and [−R,R]. This scalar function is continuous on a compact box and bounded there, hence integrable for that finite product measure. M002 now gives
∫_Q ∂_{x_j}g dx=∫_{Qrest}(∫_{[−R,R]}∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)) dr) dy=0
by F002. When n=1, Qrest is the singleton ℝ^0 of measure one, so this formula reduces to the very same one-variable identity. Outside Q all terms in F001 vanish. Integrating F001 over ℝ^n, using the finiteness of both summand integrals and symmetry of the dot product, yields
∫_{ℝ^n}∂_{x_j}u(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t0) dx=−∫_{ℝ^n}u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_jx_j}u(x,t0) dx.
Quantify the arbitrary coordinate j, discharge L1, and quantify t0. This proves the claimed integration-by-parts identity including absolute integrability.

Fix real t0 and assume L1: t0>0. H002 makes all derivative notation classical. N002 proves e(·,t0) and all derivative products below are integrable, so E is the finite energy integral in D004. N003 proves differentiability and its integral formula. Substitute that formula and use N004 for each coordinate, then use finite-sum linearity and the definition of Delta:
E'(t0)=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t(x,t0)·u_tt(x,t0) dx+2Σ_{j=1}^n∫_{ℝ^n}∂_{x_j}u(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t0) dx
=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t(x,t0)·u_tt(x,t0) dx−2Σ_{j=1}^n∫_{ℝ^n}u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_jx_j}u(x,t0) dx
=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t(x,t0)·(u_tt(x,t0)−Delta u(x,t0)) dx=0.
The last equality is N001 pointwise. Every passage uses finite integrals from N002, with no boundary term left over. Discharge L1 and universally quantify t0. Hence E is differentiable everywhere on (0,∞) with E'=0 there.

Fix arbitrary real s,t and assume L2: 0<s<t. Apply M004 to the real function equal to E on positive times and zero elsewhere, with derivative function zero, and endpoints s,t. By F001, E is differentiable at every point of [s,t], so it is continuous there and has derivative zero on (s,t). M004 gives an interior point whose derivative zero equals (E(t)−E(s))/(t−s). Since t−s>0, E(t)=E(s). Discharge L2 and quantify s,t. Any pair of positive times is either equal or can be ordered in this way, so symmetry of equality gives constancy on (0,∞). Together with N002 and F001 this proves P. The density is exactly |u_t|²+Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u|² from D003, so no factor 1/2 is introduced and no assertion at time zero is used.

# Conservation of energy for a sphere-valued wave map

## Original exercise

Lawrence C. Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, second edition,
Graduate Studies in Mathematics 19, AMS, 2010, section 12.6, exercise 14,
printed page 694. The preceding exercise 13 defines the sphere-valued
wave map. ISBN: 978-0-8218-4974-3.

> 14. Prove that if \(\mathbf u\) is a wave map into the unit sphere,
> with compact support in space, we have conservation of energy:
> \[
> \frac{d}{dt}\int_{\mathbb R^n}
>       |\mathbf u_t|^2+|D\mathbf u|^2\,dx=0.
> \]

## Fixed interpretation and complete target

A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
value.conclusion: For every t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^n. The energy E:(0,∞)→ℝ is differentiable and E'(t)=0 for every t>0; consequently E is constant on (0,∞). The energy is exactly ∫_{ℝ^n}(|u_t|²+|Du|²) dx with no factor 1/2. No assertion at time zero is made.

1: # Conservation of energy for a sphere-valued wave map
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Lawrence C. Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, second edition,
6: Graduate Studies in Mathematics 19, AMS, 2010, section 12.6, exercise 14,
7: printed page 694. The preceding exercise 13 defines the sphere-valued
8: wave map. ISBN: 978-0-8218-4974-3.
9: 
10: > 14. Prove that if \(\mathbf u\) is a wave map into the unit sphere,
11: > with compact support in space, we have conservation of energy:
12: > \[
13: > \frac{d}{dt}\int_{\mathbb R^n}
14: >       |\mathbf u_t|^2+|D\mathbf u|^2\,dx=0.
15: > \]
16: 
17: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
18: 
19: A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
20: the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
21: of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
22: This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
23: correction.
24: 
25: Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
26: \(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
27: Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:
28: 
29: 1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
30: 2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
31:    \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
32:    \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
33:    assumed.
34: 3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
35:    \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
36:    \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).
37: 
38: With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define
39: 
40: \[
41: e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
42: \qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
43: \]
44: 
45: The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
46: \(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
47: Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
48: and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
49: 
50: ## Fixed natural-language proof
51: 
52: ### 1. Tangency and the wave-map equation
53: 
54: Differentiate \(u\cdot u=1\) in time. The product rule gives
55: \(2u\cdot u_t=0\), so
56: 
57: \[
58: u\cdot u_t=0,\qquad
59: u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)=a(u_t\cdot u)=0.          \tag{1}
60: \]
61: 
62: No derivative of \(a\) is needed. The familiar explicit equation also
63: follows from the assumptions: twice differentiating the unit constraint
64: gives \(u\cdot u_{tt}=-|u_t|^2\) and
65: \(u\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u=-|\partial_{x_j}u|^2\).
66: Dotting the normality equation with \(u\), using \(|u|^2=1\), yields
67: \(a=\sum_j|\partial_{x_j}u|^2-|u_t|^2\). This is a consequence,
68: not an additional PDE assumption.
69: 
70: ### 2. Common compact support and integrability
71: 
72: Fix \(t_0>0\), put \(J=[t_0/2,3t_0/2]\), and choose its compact
73: spatial set \(C\) from assumption 3. Since \(C\) is bounded, choose
74: \(R>0\) with \(C\subset(-R,R)^n\) and set \(Q=[-R,R]^n\).
75: The box has finite Lebesgue measure \((2R)^n\).
76: 
77: On the open set \((\mathbb R^n\setminus C)\times\operatorname{int}J\),
78: the map equals the constant \(q\), so all its positive-order
79: derivatives vanish. At interior times, \(e\), \(e_t\), and the
80: derivative products used below consequently vanish outside \(C\).
81: They are continuous by smoothness; their spatial sections are measurable,
82: bounded on \(Q\), and supported there. Their absolute integrals are
83: bounded by a finite constant times \(|Q|\). This proves integrability
84: of \(e(\cdot,t_0)\) and of all later terms. Since \(t_0\) was arbitrary,
85: the energy is a finite, well-defined integral at every positive time.
86: 
87: ### 3. Differentiate the energy integral
88: 
89: The product rule and equality of mixed derivatives give
90: 
91: \[
92: e_t=2u_t\cdot u_{tt}
93:    +2\sum_{j=1}^n\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t.           \tag{2}
94: \]
95: 
96: Choose \(\eta>0\) so that
97: \([t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\subset\operatorname{int}J\).
98: Continuity of (2) on the compact box
99: \(Q\times[t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\) gives a finite bound \(|e_t|\leq B\).
100: For \(0<|h|<\eta\), the one-variable mean value theorem at fixed
101: \(x\) therefore gives
102: 
103: \[
104: \left|\frac{e(x,t_0+h)-e(x,t_0)}h\right|
105: \leq B\mathbf1_Q(x).
106: \]
107: 
108: Outside \(Q\), both densities vanish, so the bound holds throughout
109: \(\mathbb R^n\). The right side is integrable. The difference
110: quotients converge pointwise to \(e_t(x,t_0)\). Dominated convergence
111: and linearity for these integrable functions now prove
112: 
113: \[
114: E'(t_0)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e_t(x,t_0)\,dx.            \tag{3}
115: \]
116: 
117: This establishes differentiability of the actual finite integral.
118: 
119: ### 4. Integration by parts and cancellation
120: 
121: For each spatial index \(j\), at time \(t_0\) put
122: \(g_j(x)=u_t(x,t_0)\cdot\partial_{x_j}u(x,t_0)\).
123: It is smooth and vanishes on a neighborhood of the boundary of \(Q\),
124: because \(C\subset\operatorname{int}Q\). The product rule gives
125: 
126: \[
127: \partial_{x_j}g_j
128: =\partial_{x_j}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_j}u
129:  +u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u.
130: \]
131: 
132: Integrate first over \(x_j\in[-R,R]\) at fixed remaining coordinates.
133: The fundamental theorem of calculus gives zero because both endpoint
134: values of \(g_j\) are zero. Fubini applies on \(Q\) because the
135: derivative and its two summands are continuous and bounded on a
136: finite-measure box. Thus \(\int_Q\partial_{x_j}g_j=0\).
137: All these terms vanish outside \(Q\), so
138: 
139: \[
140: \int_{\mathbb R^n}\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t\,dx
141: =-\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u\,dx.              \tag{4}
142: \]
143: 
144: Every integral is finite by step 2. Sum (4) over the finitely many
145: spatial indices and substitute (2) into (3):
146: 
147: \[
148: \begin{aligned}
149: E'(t_0)
150: &=2\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot u_{tt}\,dx
151:  -2\sum_{j=1}^n\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u\,dx\\
152: &=2\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)\,dx=0,
153: \end{aligned}
154: \]
155: 
156: by (1). This holds at every \(t_0>0\). Hence \(E\) is differentiable
157: with zero derivative on \((0,\infty)\), and is constant there by the
158: mean value theorem. This is conservation of energy with exactly the
159: normalization in the exercise.
160:

Fix real t0 and assume L1: t0>0. Put J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. Its endpoints satisfy 0<t0/2<3t0/2<∞, so H006 provides a compact spatial set for that entire interval. H001 gives finite positive integer dimensions throughout.

Choose such a C from F001. A compact subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space is bounded; enlarging a bound gives a positive real R such that C⊂(−R,R)^n. Compactness also makes C closed, hence (ℝ^n\C)×int J is open. On this open set u=q. By H002 and the local derivative of a constant, every positive-order spatial or time derivative of u vanishes there. Differentiating a constant here uses the fixed vector q and requires no condition on its norm.

Choose R as in F002 and put Q=[−R,R]^n. It is compact and has finite Lebesgue measure |Q|=(2R)^n. By smoothness H002, finite sums and products of the derivatives occurring in e, e_t, u_t·u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u, u_t·∂_{x_j}u and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u) are continuous, and e,e_t are jointly smooth. At every fixed r∈int J each listed spatial function vanishes outside C by F003, and is bounded on Q by continuity on a compact set. Continuous real functions on ℝ^n are measurable; a bound on Q and zero values outside Q dominate their absolute values by a finite constant times the indicator of Q. That indicator is integrable with integral (2R)^n, so each function is absolutely integrable. This applies to every spatial coordinate j with 1≤j≤n, and to every r∈int J.

Define η=t0/4>0. Then [t0−η,t0+η]=[3t0/4,5t0/4]⊂(t0/2,3t0/2)=int J. The continuous real function |e_t| on the compact nonempty set Q×[t0−η,t0+η] is bounded. Taking a nonnegative bound proves that there exists B≥0 with |e_t(x,r)|≤B for every x∈Q and every r in this closed time interval.

Choose B from F004. The witnesses C,R,η,B and defined J,Q have all the asserted common-support, measure, regularity, integrability and bound properties by F001,F002,F003,F005,F004. In particular t0∈int J and e(·,t0) is integrable. Introduce the existential quantifiers over C,R,η,B before closing their scope; discharge L1 and universally quantify the arbitrary t0. This proves the detailed common-support assertion and, by the arbitrariness of the positive base time, integrability of e(·,t) for every t>0.

Fix real t0 and temporarily assume L1: t0>0. Instantiate N002 to choose jointly C,R,η,B, and set J=[t0/2,3t0/2], Q=[−R,R]^n as in that statement. In particular the indicated time window lies in int J. By H002 the product rule and equality of mixed coordinate derivatives give, at every (x,t) with t>0,
e_t(x,t)=2u_t(x,t)·u_tt(x,t)+2Σ_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_j}u(x,t)·∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t).
N002 makes every term on the right integrable at each such time.

For each fixed spatial point x∈Q and each real nonzero increment h0 with |h0|<η, apply M004 to the real function of time r↦e(x,r), extended by zero on nonpositive times, and its derivative r↦e_t(x,r) on positive times (also assigned zero elsewhere). Use the ordered endpoints min(t0,t0+h0), max(t0,t0+h0). Their closed interval lies inside [t0−η,t0+η]⊂int J, where smoothness gives continuity and the stated derivative. M004 gives an intermediate derivative equal to the secant slope. For either sign of h0 that slope is (e(x,t0+h0)−e(x,t0))/h0. The uniform bound in N002 therefore gives its absolute value at most B. Outside Q both densities are zero by N002. Thus throughout ℝ^n,
|(e(x,t0+h0)−e(x,t0))/h0|≤B 1_Q(x).
The right side is integrable, since Q has finite measure and B is finite and nonnegative.

Take an arbitrary real sequence h and temporarily assume L2: for every natural k, 0<|h(k)|<η, and h(k)→0. Define V(k)(x)=(e(x,t0+h(k))−e(x,t0))/h(k) and w(x)=B 1_Q(x). Each V(k) is a continuous real function of x, hence strongly measurable and in particular almost everywhere strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure; it is integrable either by N002 and linearity or by F002. By F002, |V(k)(x)|≤w(x) everywhere, and w is integrable. By the pointwise time differentiability supplied by smoothness, V(k)(x)→e_t(x,t0) for every x. All these facts concern the real codomain and the Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n.

Apply M001 with its measure space ℝ^n with Lebesgue measure, codomain ℝ, sequence V, limit x↦e_t(x,t0), and bound w. The four analytic premises were proved in F003, and ℝ has the required real normed-space structure. It follows that ∫ V(k)(x) dx→∫ e_t(x,t0) dx. N002 and D004 identify, by linearity of finite integrals, ∫ V(k)(x) dx=(E(t0+h(k))−E(t0))/h(k). Discharge L2 and quantify the arbitrary sequence h: every sequence of nonzero increments in this punctured η-window tending to zero gives energy quotients tending to ∫ e_t(x,t0) dx.

F004 implies the full punctured limit as the real increment tends to zero. Indeed failure of that limit would give some fixed positive error and arbitrarily small nonzero increments within the η-window whose quotient errors are at least that amount. Choosing one at distance less than 1/(k+1) for each natural k would form a sequence contradicting F004. This is the sequential criterion for limits in ℝ, with the entire window inside positive time. Thus the actual finite integral E is differentiable at t0 and
E'(t0)=∫_{ℝ^n}e_t(x,t0) dx.
Combine this with F001 and the integrability exported in N002. Discharge L1 and universally quantify t0; no choices C,R,η,B enter the conclusion. This proves the claimed derivative formula and integrability.

Fix real t0 and assume L1: t0>0, and fix any spatial coordinate j with 1≤j≤n (H001). Choose C,R from N002 at this time and set Q=[−R,R]^n. Put g(x)=u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u(x,t0). It is smooth by H002. Since C is compact and contained in the open box (−R,R)^n, it has positive distance from the boundary of Q; N002 therefore makes g zero on a neighborhood of that boundary. The product rule gives
∂_{x_j}g(x)=∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u(x,t0)+u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_jx_j}u(x,t0).
N002 says the derivative and each summand are continuous, supported in C, and integrable on ℝ^n and hence on Q.

Let iota(y,r) insert the real r in coordinate j, with y∈ℝ^(n−1) giving all remaining coordinates in their original order, and put phi(y)(r)=g(iota(y,r)). For each y, phi(y) is smooth on ℝ with derivative r↦∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)). Its endpoint values at −R and R are zero, since those points have a coordinate on the boundary of Q and in any event lie outside C. Apply M003 with real codomain, endpoints −R,R, function phi(y), and the displayed derivative. The derivative exists at every point of [−R,R] and is continuous, hence interval integrable there. We obtain
∫_{−R}^{R} ∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)) dr=phi(y)(R)−phi(y)(−R)=0.
This holds for every y∈ℝ^(n−1). The oriented integral agrees with the Lebesgue integral on the closed interval here, since −R<R and the endpoints have measure zero.

Set Qrest=[−R,R]^(n−1). Under iota, Qrest×[−R,R] is exactly Q with its coordinates reordered. Standard Lebesgue measure is the product of the coordinate measures (D001); reordering these factors preserves the measure, since on any coordinate rectangle both descriptions give the product of the same side lengths. Thus the integral on Q is the product-measure integral of (y,r)↦∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)) with Lebesgue measures restricted to Qrest and [−R,R]. This scalar function is continuous on a compact box and bounded there, hence integrable for that finite product measure. M002 now gives
∫_Q ∂_{x_j}g dx=∫_{Qrest}(∫_{[−R,R]}∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)) dr) dy=0
by F002. When n=1, Qrest is the singleton ℝ^0 of measure one, so this formula reduces to the very same one-variable identity. Outside Q all terms in F001 vanish. Integrating F001 over ℝ^n, using the finiteness of both summand integrals and symmetry of the dot product, yields
∫_{ℝ^n}∂_{x_j}u(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t0) dx=−∫_{ℝ^n}u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_jx_j}u(x,t0) dx.
Quantify the arbitrary coordinate j, discharge L1, and quantify t0. This proves the claimed integration-by-parts identity including absolute integrability.

Fix real t0 and assume L1: t0>0. H002 makes all derivative notation classical. N002 proves e(·,t0) and all derivative products below are integrable, so E is the finite energy integral in D004. N003 proves differentiability and its integral formula. Substitute that formula and use N004 for each coordinate, then use finite-sum linearity and the definition of Delta:
E'(t0)=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t(x,t0)·u_tt(x,t0) dx+2Σ_{j=1}^n∫_{ℝ^n}∂_{x_j}u(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t0) dx
=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t(x,t0)·u_tt(x,t0) dx−2Σ_{j=1}^n∫_{ℝ^n}u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_jx_j}u(x,t0) dx
=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t(x,t0)·(u_tt(x,t0)−Delta u(x,t0)) dx=0.
The last equality is N001 pointwise. Every passage uses finite integrals from N002, with no boundary term left over. Discharge L1 and universally quantify t0. Hence E is differentiable everywhere on (0,∞) with E'=0 there.

Fix arbitrary real s,t and assume L2: 0<s<t. Apply M004 to the real function equal to E on positive times and zero elsewhere, with derivative function zero, and endpoints s,t. By F001, E is differentiable at every point of [s,t], so it is continuous there and has derivative zero on (s,t). M004 gives an interior point whose derivative zero equals (E(t)−E(s))/(t−s). Since t−s>0, E(t)=E(s). Discharge L2 and quantify s,t. Any pair of positive times is either equal or can be ordered in this way, so symmetry of equality gives constancy on (0,∞). Together with N002 and F001 this proves P. The density is exactly |u_t|²+Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u|² from D003, so no factor 1/2 is introduced and no assertion at time zero is used.

30: orthonormal bases for each summand in a direct sum of spaces can be combined into an orthonormal
31: basis for the whole sum in `DirectSum.IsInternal.subordinateOrthonormalBasis`. In
32: the last section, various properties of matrices are explored.

34: ## Main definitions
35: 
36: - `EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n`: defined to be `PiLp 2 (n → 𝕜)` for any `Fintype n`, i.e., the space
37:   from functions to `n` to `𝕜` with the `L²` norm. We register several instances on it (notably
38:   that it is a finite-dimensional inner product space), and provide a `!ₚ[]` notation (for numeric
39:   subscripts like `₂`) for the case when the indexing type is `Fin n`.
40: 
41: - `OrthonormalBasis 𝕜 ι`: defined to be an isometry to Euclidean space from a given
42:   finite-dimensional inner product space, `E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] EuclideanSpace 𝕜 ι`.
43: 
44: - `Basis.toOrthonormalBasis`: constructs an `OrthonormalBasis` for a finite-dimensional
45:   Euclidean space from a `Basis` which is `Orthonormal`.
46: 
47: - `Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension`: provides an existential result of an
48:   `OrthonormalBasis` extending a given orthonormal set
49: 
50: - `exists_orthonormalBasis`: provides an orthonormal basis on a finite-dimensional vector space
51: 
52: - `stdOrthonormalBasis`: provides an arbitrarily-chosen `OrthonormalBasis` of a given
53:   finite-dimensional inner product space
54: 
55: - `orthonormalBasisSingleton`: an orthonormal basis formed by a single unit vector in a
56:   one-dimensional inner product space.
57: 
58: For consequences in infinite dimension (Hilbert bases, etc.), see the file
59: `Analysis.InnerProductSpace.L2Space`.

abbrev WM.Space (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ
abbrev WM.Target (m : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)

def WM.smoothOrder : WithTop ℕ∞ := ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)
def WM.positive (n : ℕ) : Set (WM.Domain n) := {p | 0 < p.2}
def WM.box (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (WM.Space n) := Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Icc (-R) R)
def WM.openBox (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (WM.Space n) := Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Ioo (-R) R)
def WM.timeBand (t : ℝ) : Set ℝ := Set.Icc (t / 2) (3 * t / 2)

noncomputable def WM.dt {n : ℕ} {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    (f : WM.Domain n → F) (p : WM.Domain n) : F :=
  fderiv ℝ f p (0, 1)
noncomputable def WM.dx {n : ℕ} {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    (f : WM.Domain n → F) (j : Fin n) (p : WM.Domain n) : F :=
  fderiv ℝ f p (Pi.single j 1, 0)
noncomputable def WM.dtt {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) := WM.dt (WM.dt u)
noncomputable def WM.dxx {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (j : Fin n) := WM.dx (WM.dx u j) j
noncomputable def WM.lap {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (p : WM.Domain n) := ∑ j, WM.dxx u j p
noncomputable def WM.gradSq {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j, ‖WM.dx u j p‖ ^ 2
noncomputable def WM.density {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  ‖WM.dt u p‖ ^ 2 + WM.gradSq u p
noncomputable def WM.densityT {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) := WM.dt (WM.density u)
noncomputable def WM.energy {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x : WM.Space n, WM.density u (x, t)
noncomputable def WM.accelProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (WM.dt u p) (WM.dtt u p)
noncomputable def WM.gradProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (j : Fin n) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (WM.dx u j p) (WM.dx (WM.dt u) j p)
noncomputable def WM.lapProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (j : Fin n) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (WM.dt u p) (WM.dxx u j p)
noncomputable def WM.flux {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (j : Fin n) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (WM.dt u p) (WM.dx u j p)

def WM.fields {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) : Set (WM.Domain n → ℝ) :=
  {f | f = WM.density u ∨ f = WM.densityT u ∨ f = WM.accelProduct u ∨
    ∃ j : Fin n, f = WM.gradProduct u j ∨ f = WM.lapProduct u j ∨
      f = WM.flux u j ∨ f = WM.dx (WM.flux u j) j}

def WM.sectionGood {n : ℕ} (f : WM.Domain n → ℝ) (C Q : Set (WM.Space n)) (t : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous (fun x => f (x, t)) ∧ Function.support (fun x => f (x, t)) ⊆ C ∧
  (∃ b : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ Q, |f (x, t)| ≤ b) ∧
  Measurable (fun x => f (x, t)) ∧ Integrable (fun x => f (x, t))

def WM.commonSupport {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (q : WM.Target m)
    (t : ℝ) (C : Set (WM.Space n)) (R η B : ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsCompact C ∧ 0 < R ∧ 0 < η ∧ 0 ≤ B ∧ C ⊆ WM.openBox n R ∧
  volume (WM.box n R) = ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * R) ^ n) ∧
  volume (WM.box n R) < ⊤ ∧
  Set.Icc (t - η) (t + η) ⊆ interior (WM.timeBand t) ∧
  (∀ x r, x ∉ C → r ∈ WM.timeBand t → u (x, r) = q) ∧
  (∀ x r, x ∉ C → r ∈ interior (WM.timeBand t) →
    ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k u (x, r) = 0) ∧
  (∀ r ∈ interior (WM.timeBand t), ∀ f ∈ WM.fields u, WM.sectionGood f C (WM.box n R) r) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ WM.box n R, ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc (t - η) (t + η), |WM.densityT u (x, r)| ≤ B)

def WM.supportFacts {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (q : WM.Target m) : Prop :=
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Integrable (fun x => WM.density u (x, t))) ∧
  ContDiffOn ℝ WM.smoothOrder (WM.density u) (WM.positive n) ∧
  ContDiffOn ℝ WM.smoothOrder (WM.densityT u) (WM.positive n) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ∃ C : Set (WM.Space n), ∃ R η B : ℝ, WM.commonSupport u q t C R η B)

def WM.tangency {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) : Prop :=
  ∀ x t, 0 < t →
    inner ℝ (u (x,t)) (WM.dt u (x,t)) = 0 ∧
    inner ℝ (WM.dt u (x,t)) (WM.dtt u (x,t) - WM.lap u (x,t)) = 0 ∧
    inner ℝ (u (x,t)) (WM.dtt u (x,t)) = -(‖WM.dt u (x,t)‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin n, inner ℝ (u (x,t)) (WM.dxx u j (x,t)) = -(‖WM.dx u j (x,t)‖ ^ 2)) ∧
    (∀ a : ℝ, WM.dtt u (x,t) - WM.lap u (x,t) = a • u (x,t) →
      a = WM.gradSq u (x,t) - ‖WM.dt u (x,t)‖ ^ 2) ∧
    WM.dtt u (x,t) - WM.lap u (x,t) =
      (WM.gradSq u (x,t) - ‖WM.dt u (x,t)‖ ^ 2) • u (x,t)

def WM.energyDerivative {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) : Prop :=
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t →
    HasDerivAt (WM.energy u) (∫ x : WM.Space n, WM.densityT u (x,t)) t) ∧
  (∀ x t, 0 < t → WM.densityT u (x,t) =
    2 * WM.accelProduct u (x,t) + 2 * ∑ j, WM.gradProduct u j (x,t)) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t →
    Integrable (fun x => WM.densityT u (x,t)) ∧
    Integrable (fun x => WM.accelProduct u (x,t)) ∧
    ∀ j : Fin n, Integrable (fun x => WM.gradProduct u j (x,t)))

def WM.integrationByParts {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ∀ j : Fin n,
    Integrable (fun x => WM.gradProduct u j (x,t)) ∧
    Integrable (fun x => WM.lapProduct u j (x,t)) ∧
    (∫ x : WM.Space n, WM.gradProduct u j (x,t)) =
      -(∫ x : WM.Space n, WM.lapProduct u j (x,t))

def WM.conservation {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) : Prop :=
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Integrable (fun x => WM.density u (x,t))) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → HasDerivAt (WM.energy u) 0 t) ∧
  (∀ s t : ℝ, 0 < s → 0 < t → WM.energy u s = WM.energy u t)

import Mathlib
open scoped BigOperators
open MeasureTheory Set Filter Topology

abbrev WM.Space (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ
abbrev WM.Target (m : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)
abbrev WM.Domain (n : ℕ) := WM.Space n × ℝ

def WM.smoothOrder : WithTop ℕ∞ := ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)
def WM.positive (n : ℕ) : Set (WM.Domain n) := {p | 0 < p.2}
def WM.box (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (WM.Space n) := Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Icc (-R) R)
def WM.openBox (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (WM.Space n) := Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Ioo (-R) R)
def WM.timeBand (t : ℝ) : Set ℝ := Set.Icc (t / 2) (3 * t / 2)

noncomputable def WM.dt {n : ℕ} {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    (f : WM.Domain n → F) (p : WM.Domain n) : F :=
  fderiv ℝ f p (0, 1)
noncomputable def WM.dx {n : ℕ} {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    (f : WM.Domain n → F) (j : Fin n) (p : WM.Domain n) : F :=
  fderiv ℝ f p (Pi.single j 1, 0)
noncomputable def WM.dtt {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) := WM.dt (WM.dt u)
noncomputable def WM.dxx {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (j : Fin n) := WM.dx (WM.dx u j) j
noncomputable def WM.lap {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (p : WM.Domain n) := ∑ j, WM.dxx u j p
noncomputable def WM.gradSq {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j, ‖WM.dx u j p‖ ^ 2
noncomputable def WM.density {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  ‖WM.dt u p‖ ^ 2 + WM.gradSq u p
noncomputable def WM.densityT {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) := WM.dt (WM.density u)
noncomputable def WM.energy {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x : WM.Space n, WM.density u (x, t)
noncomputable def WM.accelProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (WM.dt u p) (WM.dtt u p)
noncomputable def WM.gradProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (j : Fin n) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (WM.dx u j p) (WM.dx (WM.dt u) j p)
noncomputable def WM.lapProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (j : Fin n) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (WM.dt u p) (WM.dxx u j p)
noncomputable def WM.flux {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (j : Fin n) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (WM.dt u p) (WM.dx u j p)

def WM.fields {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) : Set (WM.Domain n → ℝ) :=
  {f | f = WM.density u ∨ f = WM.densityT u ∨ f = WM.accelProduct u ∨
    ∃ j : Fin n, f = WM.gradProduct u j ∨ f = WM.lapProduct u j ∨
      f = WM.flux u j ∨ f = WM.dx (WM.flux u j) j}

def WM.sectionGood {n : ℕ} (f : WM.Domain n → ℝ) (C Q : Set (WM.Space n)) (t : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous (fun x => f (x, t)) ∧ Function.support (fun x => f (x, t)) ⊆ C ∧
  (∃ b : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ Q, |f (x, t)| ≤ b) ∧
  Measurable (fun x => f (x, t)) ∧ Integrable (fun x => f (x, t))

def WM.commonSupport {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (q : WM.Target m)
    (t : ℝ) (C : Set (WM.Space n)) (R η B : ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsCompact C ∧ 0 < R ∧ 0 < η ∧ 0 ≤ B ∧ C ⊆ WM.openBox n R ∧
  volume (WM.box n R) = ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * R) ^ n) ∧
  volume (WM.box n R) < ⊤ ∧
  Set.Icc (t - η) (t + η) ⊆ interior (WM.timeBand t) ∧
  (∀ x r, x ∉ C → r ∈ WM.timeBand t → u (x, r) = q) ∧
  (∀ x r, x ∉ C → r ∈ interior (WM.timeBand t) →
    ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k u (x, r) = 0) ∧
  (∀ r ∈ interior (WM.timeBand t), ∀ f ∈ WM.fields u, WM.sectionGood f C (WM.box n R) r) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ WM.box n R, ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc (t - η) (t + η), |WM.densityT u (x, r)| ≤ B)

def WM.supportFacts {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (q : WM.Target m) : Prop :=
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Integrable (fun x => WM.density u (x, t))) ∧
  ContDiffOn ℝ WM.smoothOrder (WM.density u) (WM.positive n) ∧
  ContDiffOn ℝ WM.smoothOrder (WM.densityT u) (WM.positive n) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ∃ C : Set (WM.Space n), ∃ R η B : ℝ, WM.commonSupport u q t C R η B)

def WM.tangency {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) : Prop :=
  ∀ x t, 0 < t →
    inner ℝ (u (x,t)) (WM.dt u (x,t)) = 0 ∧
    inner ℝ (WM.dt u (x,t)) (WM.dtt u (x,t) - WM.lap u (x,t)) = 0 ∧
    inner ℝ (u (x,t)) (WM.dtt u (x,t)) = -(‖WM.dt u (x,t)‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin n, inner ℝ (u (x,t)) (WM.dxx u j (x,t)) = -(‖WM.dx u j (x,t)‖ ^ 2)) ∧
    (∀ a : ℝ, WM.dtt u (x,t) - WM.lap u (x,t) = a • u (x,t) →
      a = WM.gradSq u (x,t) - ‖WM.dt u (x,t)‖ ^ 2) ∧
    WM.dtt u (x,t) - WM.lap u (x,t) =
      (WM.gradSq u (x,t) - ‖WM.dt u (x,t)‖ ^ 2) • u (x,t)

def WM.energyDerivative {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) : Prop :=
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t →
    HasDerivAt (WM.energy u) (∫ x : WM.Space n, WM.densityT u (x,t)) t) ∧
  (∀ x t, 0 < t → WM.densityT u (x,t) =
    2 * WM.accelProduct u (x,t) + 2 * ∑ j, WM.gradProduct u j (x,t)) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t →
    Integrable (fun x => WM.densityT u (x,t)) ∧
    Integrable (fun x => WM.accelProduct u (x,t)) ∧
    ∀ j : Fin n, Integrable (fun x => WM.gradProduct u j (x,t)))

def WM.integrationByParts {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ∀ j : Fin n,
    Integrable (fun x => WM.gradProduct u j (x,t)) ∧
    Integrable (fun x => WM.lapProduct u j (x,t)) ∧
    (∫ x : WM.Space n, WM.gradProduct u j (x,t)) =
      -(∫ x : WM.Space n, WM.lapProduct u j (x,t))

def WM.conservation {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) : Prop :=
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Integrable (fun x => WM.density u (x,t))) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → HasDerivAt (WM.energy u) 0 t) ∧
  (∀ s t : ℝ, 0 < s → 0 < t → WM.energy u s = WM.energy u t)

The spatial Pi type carries the sup norm; this gives the same topology, compact sets and Fréchet derivative as the Euclidean norm in finite dimension, so it changes no domain or analytic assertion. It is the sole spatial representation used in the proof. The actual volume_pi declaration identifies volume with the product of real Lebesgue measures, including the measure-one empty product. Encode u on WM.Space n × ℝ with H002 smooth only on the open set t>0. Restriction gives the original positive-time map; conversely any original map has an arbitrary extension (e.g. value q at nonpositive times). Every hypothesis and conclusion is restricted to positive times, and all derivatives depend only on the germ there, so these operations are inverse at the level of the stated theorem. import Mathlib
open scoped BigOperators
open MeasureTheory Set Filter Topology

abbrev WM.Space (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ
abbrev WM.Target (m : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)
abbrev WM.Domain (n : ℕ) := WM.Space n × ℝ

def WM.smoothOrder : WithTop ℕ∞ := ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)
def WM.positive (n : ℕ) : Set (WM.Domain n) := {p | 0 < p.2}
def WM.box (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (WM.Space n) := Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Icc (-R) R)
def WM.openBox (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (WM.Space n) := Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Ioo (-R) R)
def WM.timeBand (t : ℝ) : Set ℝ := Set.Icc (t / 2) (3 * t / 2)

noncomputable def WM.dt {n : ℕ} {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    (f : WM.Domain n → F) (p : WM.Domain n) : F :=
  fderiv ℝ f p (0, 1)
noncomputable def WM.dx {n : ℕ} {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    (f : WM.Domain n → F) (j : Fin n) (p : WM.Domain n) : F :=
  fderiv ℝ f p (Pi.single j 1, 0)
noncomputable def WM.dtt {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) := WM.dt (WM.dt u)
noncomputable def WM.dxx {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (j : Fin n) := WM.dx (WM.dx u j) j
noncomputable def WM.lap {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (p : WM.Domain n) := ∑ j, WM.dxx u j p
noncomputable def WM.gradSq {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j, ‖WM.dx u j p‖ ^ 2
noncomputable def WM.density {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  ‖WM.dt u p‖ ^ 2 + WM.gradSq u p
noncomputable def WM.densityT {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) := WM.dt (WM.density u)
noncomputable def WM.energy {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x : WM.Space n, WM.density u (x, t)
noncomputable def WM.accelProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (WM.dt u p) (WM.dtt u p)

import Mathlib
open scoped BigOperators
open MeasureTheory Set Filter Topology

abbrev WM.Space (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ
abbrev WM.Target (m : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)
abbrev WM.Domain (n : ℕ) := WM.Space n × ℝ

def WM.smoothOrder : WithTop ℕ∞ := ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)
def WM.positive (n : ℕ) : Set (WM.Domain n) := {p | 0 < p.2}
def WM.box (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (WM.Space n) := Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Icc (-R) R)
def WM.openBox (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (WM.Space n) := Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Ioo (-R) R)
def WM.timeBand (t : ℝ) : Set ℝ := Set.Icc (t / 2) (3 * t / 2)

noncomputable def WM.dt {n : ℕ} {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    (f : WM.Domain n → F) (p : WM.Domain n) : F :=
  fderiv ℝ f p (0, 1)
noncomputable def WM.dx {n : ℕ} {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    (f : WM.Domain n → F) (j : Fin n) (p : WM.Domain n) : F :=
  fderiv ℝ f p (Pi.single j 1, 0)
noncomputable def WM.dtt {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) := WM.dt (WM.dt u)
noncomputable def WM.dxx {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (j : Fin n) := WM.dx (WM.dx u j) j
noncomputable def WM.lap {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (p : WM.Domain n) := ∑ j, WM.dxx u j p
noncomputable def WM.gradSq {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j, ‖WM.dx u j p‖ ^ 2
noncomputable def WM.density {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  ‖WM.dt u p‖ ^ 2 + WM.gradSq u p
noncomputable def WM.densityT {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) := WM.dt (WM.density u)
noncomputable def WM.energy {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x : WM.Space n, WM.density u (x, t)
noncomputable def WM.accelProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (WM.dt u p) (WM.dtt u p)
noncomputable def WM.gradProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (j : Fin n) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (WM.dx u j p) (WM.dx (WM.dt u) j p)
noncomputable def WM.lapProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (j : Fin n) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (WM.dt u p) (WM.dxx u j p)
noncomputable def WM.flux {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (j : Fin n) (p : WM.Domain n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (WM.dt u p) (WM.dx u j p)

def WM.fields {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) : Set (WM.Domain n → ℝ) :=
  {f | f = WM.density u ∨ f = WM.densityT u ∨ f = WM.accelProduct u ∨
    ∃ j : Fin n, f = WM.gradProduct u j ∨ f = WM.lapProduct u j ∨
      f = WM.flux u j ∨ f = WM.dx (WM.flux u j) j}

def WM.sectionGood {n : ℕ} (f : WM.Domain n → ℝ) (C Q : Set (WM.Space n)) (t : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous (fun x => f (x, t)) ∧ Function.support (fun x => f (x, t)) ⊆ C ∧
  (∃ b : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ Q, |f (x, t)| ≤ b) ∧
  Measurable (fun x => f (x, t)) ∧ Integrable (fun x => f (x, t))

def WM.commonSupport {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (q : WM.Target m)
    (t : ℝ) (C : Set (WM.Space n)) (R η B : ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsCompact C ∧ 0 < R ∧ 0 < η ∧ 0 ≤ B ∧ C ⊆ WM.openBox n R ∧
  volume (WM.box n R) = ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * R) ^ n) ∧
  volume (WM.box n R) < ⊤ ∧
  Set.Icc (t - η) (t + η) ⊆ interior (WM.timeBand t) ∧
  (∀ x r, x ∉ C → r ∈ WM.timeBand t → u (x, r) = q) ∧
  (∀ x r, x ∉ C → r ∈ interior (WM.timeBand t) →
    ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k u (x, r) = 0) ∧
  (∀ r ∈ interior (WM.timeBand t), ∀ f ∈ WM.fields u, WM.sectionGood f C (WM.box n R) r) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ WM.box n R, ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc (t - η) (t + η), |WM.densityT u (x, r)| ≤ B)

def WM.supportFacts {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (q : WM.Target m) : Prop :=
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Integrable (fun x => WM.density u (x, t))) ∧
  ContDiffOn ℝ WM.smoothOrder (WM.density u) (WM.positive n) ∧
  ContDiffOn ℝ WM.smoothOrder (WM.densityT u) (WM.positive n) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ∃ C : Set (WM.Space n), ∃ R η B : ℝ, WM.commonSupport u q t C R η B)

def WM.tangency {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) : Prop :=
  ∀ x t, 0 < t →
    inner ℝ (u (x,t)) (WM.dt u (x,t)) = 0 ∧
    inner ℝ (WM.dt u (x,t)) (WM.dtt u (x,t) - WM.lap u (x,t)) = 0 ∧
    inner ℝ (u (x,t)) (WM.dtt u (x,t)) = -(‖WM.dt u (x,t)‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin n, inner ℝ (u (x,t)) (WM.dxx u j (x,t)) = -(‖WM.dx u j (x,t)‖ ^ 2)) ∧
    (∀ a : ℝ, WM.dtt u (x,t) - WM.lap u (x,t) = a • u (x,t) →
      a = WM.gradSq u (x,t) - ‖WM.dt u (x,t)‖ ^ 2) ∧
    WM.dtt u (x,t) - WM.lap u (x,t) =
      (WM.gradSq u (x,t) - ‖WM.dt u (x,t)‖ ^ 2) • u (x,t)

def WM.energyDerivative {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) : Prop :=
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t →
    HasDerivAt (WM.energy u) (∫ x : WM.Space n, WM.densityT u (x,t)) t) ∧
  (∀ x t, 0 < t → WM.densityT u (x,t) =
    2 * WM.accelProduct u (x,t) + 2 * ∑ j, WM.gradProduct u j (x,t)) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t →
    Integrable (fun x => WM.densityT u (x,t)) ∧
    Integrable (fun x => WM.accelProduct u (x,t)) ∧
    ∀ j : Fin n, Integrable (fun x => WM.gradProduct u j (x,t)))

def WM.integrationByParts {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ∀ j : Fin n,
    Integrable (fun x => WM.gradProduct u j (x,t)) ∧
    Integrable (fun x => WM.lapProduct u j (x,t)) ∧
    (∫ x : WM.Space n, WM.gradProduct u j (x,t)) =
      -(∫ x : WM.Space n, WM.lapProduct u j (x,t))

def WM.conservation {n m : ℕ} (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) : Prop :=
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Integrable (fun x => WM.density u (x,t))) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → HasDerivAt (WM.energy u) 0 t) ∧
  (∀ s t : ℝ, 0 < s → 0 < t → WM.energy u s = WM.energy u t)
